subject.title: feat(feeds): add publisher following control UI

question: Should signed publisher following become a permanent OpenClaw core protocol, scheduler, database, CLI, and Control UI feature, or should ClawHub own it through plugin/package surfaces with only generic extension seams added to core?
rationale: The patch can be technically coherent under either ownership model, but repository policy strongly prefers plugins for optional ClawHub capability while the proposed implementation creates lasting core compatibility and security obligations; automation cannot choose that product boundary.

options.title: Move ownership to ClawHub
options.body: Keep only missing generic extension contracts in core and implement publisher-feed policy, scheduling, persistence, and UI integration in a ClawHub-owned plugin or package.

options.title: Sponsor the core feature
options.body: Explicitly accept permanent core ownership and require documented RPC, database, upgrade, security, and release contracts before landing the stack.

options.title: Pause the stack
options.body: Hold or close the stacked PRs until an RFC or maintainer decision establishes ownership and landing order.

recommendation.title: Move ownership to ClawHub
recommendation.body: Keep only missing generic extension contracts in core and implement publisher-feed policy, scheduling, persistence, and UI integration in a ClawHub-owned plugin or package.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans core architecture, Gateway contracts, persistent state, CLI, UI, and repository product direction rather than only ClawHub implementation details.
